title: Two forms of failure probability
statement: Let $f:\\{-1,1\\}^n\\to\\{\\pm1\\}$ be a Boolean function, let $\\delta\\in\\mathbb R$, and let $k$ be a natural number. The coordinate-switching failure probability, summed over coordinate restrictions with each free coordinate assigned weight $\\delta$ and each of the two fixed states assigned weight $(1-\\delta)/2$, equals the expected failure indicator obtained by first choosing a free-coordinate set with weight $\\delta^{|J|}(1-\\delta)^{n-|J|}$ and then choosing signs on the remaining coordinates uniformly.
hypotheses_covered: Boolean function on the n-dimensional sign cube
